Onboarding-composition — Wave 2 strategy

Epic: onboarding-composition-epic · Wave: 2 · Phase: SURVEYING · Model: Opus-only (Fable exhausted) · Opened: 2026-07-14

This Paper is the wave's living story. Strategize opened it; Digest appends the survey digest + verify plan; Decide appends decisions + the wave plan + the fresh charter; Review closes it as the debrief. Fan-out workers never write here — they write their own bp task; the next Fable folds their reports in.

The wish (verbatim intent)

Wave 1 landed grade A- (paper bp-onboarding-composition-wave-2026-07-13): the ONE-transaction ONE-receipt onboarding — nothing → authenticated → MCP-connected → correct-team instance → a proven read-only tool call, under 5 min, never printing the bearer. Wave 2 ships the identity-composition slices already filed and ready:

  • BP-ONB-02/03 — Team-aware CLI identity: bp teams / bp team use + --team instance credentials, so a user selects and pins the right team's instance.
  • BP-ONB-04 — Provision with BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL: so the Cloud-to-Studio login button actually renders.
  • BP-ONB-05/12 — Instance-ID identity: URL aliases + BOM-tolerant config parsing + a whoami receipt (instance ID, team, URL+aliases, auth tier, MCP tool-catalog version+names, read-only call result, exact client-reload instruction).

Ground every slice in the wave-1 paper and the epic's filed child tasks. Each slice needs a behavioral proof — a real first-time flow, Windows/BOM path included.

Strategic direction

The finished experience: a first-time Windows user, coming from Barkpark Cloud, runs bp once and the CLI knows who they are, which team they belong to, and which instance is that team's — with no phantom "-2" duplicate servers, no config bricked by a Notepad BOM, and a single bp whoami / doctor receipt that reads back the whole identity in one honest envelope. From the Cloud side, provisioning stamps BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL so Studio renders the "sign in via Cloud" button instead of a dead corner. Identity becomes composed and legible end-to-end, not scattered across URL-string keys.

The load-bearing reconciliation (surveyors must nail this first): the epic task's wave_status claims wave 1 built "8/8 slices" — but the local checkout / origin main shows internal/cli/config.go with no InstanceID, no Aliases, and no BOM strip; the ServerEntry is still keyed purely by normalized URL. This matches the KNOWN failure mode of wave 1 (Decide committed to a diverged LOCAL main and never PR'd — same reason the wave-1 charter is stranded on neither origin nor local). So wave 2 likely builds the identity PLUMBING fresh, not merely activates it. Every builder must diff its target files against origin/main before writing, and treat wave-1 "done" claims as unverified until proven.

Choices I lean toward (tentative — Decide finalizes after two explore rounds):

  • Key identity by InstanceID first, URL second. Add InstanceID string + Aliases []string to ServerEntry; key Remember/Find/IsActive/DisplayName by InstanceID when known, fall back to normalized-URL only for ID-less bare local dev. A second hostname of a known instance folds into Aliases, never mints a "-2". Source of truth for the ID: the control plane's DomainStatusResult.Instance.ID + Domains[] (already modeled in internal/cloudclient/client.go).
  • Wire the ID at connect/attach (task-e6b0bc97130bae89) — plumbing is inert until a caller stamps the real ID. This is the E2E activation: one instance via two hostnames → one ServerEntry.
  • BOM tolerance is a one-line strip (bytes.TrimPrefix(raw, []byte{0xEF,0xBB,0xBF})) before Unmarshal in LoadConfig; SaveConfig already emits BOM-free JSON and self-heals. Prove it with a failing-first test (TestBOMBricksLoadConfig flips to green).
  • whoami is the receipt spine. Extend bp whoami -o json (builtins.go) to carry instance_id + aliases[] + team + auth_tier + MCP catalog version/names + read-only call result + the exact client-reload instruction. The onboarding doctor composes over this — don't fork a second receipt.
  • Team model needs a real backend concept. bp teams / bp team use presuppose the server/control-plane models teams + memberships and can mint --team-scoped instance credentials. Whether that maps to existing tenancy/workspace scoping (bp cloud members, workspace-scoped tokens) is the biggest open design question — surveyors map it before Decide commits a shape.
  • BP-ONB-04 is a provisioning + Studio-render pair: stamp BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL at provision time (cloud/**) and make the Studio session view render the Cloud login button when it's present (session_controller.ex / session_html/new.html.heex). Backfill for existing instances is a separate backlog slice.

Prioritize: (1) origin-main truth reconciliation — everything downstream depends on whether we build or activate; (2) the ServerEntry identity core (BP-ONB-05/12) since 02/03/04 all read from it; (3) the team-model design question, because it's the one slice whose backend shape is genuinely uncertain.

Constraints held: Opus-only every phase (Fable exhausted, never Haiku). No charter file exists — reconstruct epic context from the epic task + wave-1 paper; Decide writes the charter FRESH and lands it via clean-extract (detached worktree off origin/main → copy charter → commit → PR → admin-merge), NEVER pushing diverged local main. Builders commit to LOCAL worktree branches and do NOT push; the steward pushes green branches. Keep every onboarding slice FILE-DISJOINT from the concurrent cloud-build W6 cycle (wf_fe674ef4-19d) running tenancy/search.

Survey plan (in flight now)

15 broad Sonnet surveyors cast a wide net. Each question + why it changes the plan:

  1. origin-main-truth — What identity code is ACTUALLY on origin/main? Diff config.go/servers_cmd.go/builtins.go for InstanceID/Aliases/BOM/team verbs; reconcile against the "8/8 done" wave_status. Why: decides build-fresh vs activate for every slice.
  2. serverentry-config-map — Full ServerEntry struct + RememberServer/FindServer/IsActiveServer/deriveUniqueName/DisplayName-collision + LoadConfig/SaveConfig + config.json schema. Why: 02/03/05/12 all mutate this one struct.
  3. control-plane-instance-shape — cloudclient DomainStatusResult.Instance{ID} + Domains[]; which fields are live at attach/connect; how bp attach/connect call the control plane. Why: the ID source for the whole identity fix.
  4. team-model-api — Does the server/control-plane model teams + memberships? Is there a /v1/teams route? What does a --team-scoped instance credential mean concretely? Why: BP-ONB-02/03 need a real backend team concept; this is the biggest unknown.
  5. tenancy-overlap — Existing tenancy/workspace scoping + bp cloud members + workspace-scoped tokens: does bp teams/team use overlap or extend it? Why: avoid building a parallel identity store; reuse the tenancy seam if it fits.
  6. whoami-receipt-current — Current bp whoami -o json fields (builtins.go), bp servers output, bp doctor. Why: the receipt must extend these, not fork.
  7. doctor-receipt-integration — onb-w1-onboarding-doctor-receipt: is the doctor built? How does it compose the receipt? Why: whoami feeds the doctor; the reload instruction + read-only call live here.
  8. mcp-catalog-in-receipt — Where's the MCP serve / tool catalog (bp-mcp-serve epic)? How does the receipt obtain catalog version + names + a read-only call result? Why: the receipt spec demands MCP fields.
  9. bom-config-parsing — LoadConfig Unmarshal path + existing config_test.go + Windows/Notepad save behavior. Why: BP-ONB-12 BOM tolerance + the failing-first test shape.
  10. barkpark-cloud-url-provision — Where instances are provisioned with env; where BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL is set/leaked today (base_url leak); provision path in cloud/**. Why: BP-ONB-04 stamps it at provision.
  11. studio-login-button — The Studio/session view that renders the Cloud login button (session_controller.ex, session_html/new.html.heex); what condition gates it (base_url vs cloud_url). Why: BP-ONB-04 makes it render.
  12. capabilities-base-url — How the capabilities endpoint emits base_url; onb-backlog-capabilities-base-url-alias; instance-ID + aliases in capabilities. Why: whoami/receipt + Studio button read this; possible backend slice.
  13. wave1-paper-decisions — Read the wave-1 paper fully: decisions D1-D34 (esp. D4 greenfield client-side identity, D27 identity, D34 workspace-slug resolve), what the charter must encode. Why: the fresh charter + all slices must honor prior decisions.
  14. concurrent-cycle-disjointness — What files does the cloud-build W6 cycle (wf_fe674ef4-19d, tenancy/search) touch right now? Open PRs + foreign claims. Why: onboarding slices must stay file-disjoint to avoid clobber.
  15. gate-and-build-mechanics — The Go gate (CC=clang go build ./... && go vet ./internal/cli/... && go test ./internal/cli/... -count=1); how internal/cli tests run; any Studio/api gate for BP-ONB-04; worktree isolation recipe. Why: builders need an exact, reproducible gate + isolation recipe.

Driven tasks

  • onboarding-composition-epic — epic anchor (carries wave_status + wave_paper)
  • onb-w1-team-aware-cli-identity — BP-ONB-02/03 (+BP-ONB-12 config half, whoami receipt)
  • onb-w1-instance-id-aliases-receipt — BP-ONB-05/12 plumbing
  • task-e6b0bc97130bae89 — BP-ONB-05 connect/attach ID-stamp activation (D4 wiring)
  • onb-backlog-cloud-url-fleet-backfill — BP-ONB-04 backfill BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL + fix base_url leak
  • onb-backlog-capabilities-base-url-alias — backend base_url from instance-ID + aliases

Digest — survey folded, verify fleet in flight

Phase: Digest -> Verify. 15 survey reports folded. This section states what the survey established, where reports (and the direction) were wrong, what the coverage map found vs did NOT find, and the last exploration round now flying before the plan is cut.

The one reframe that changes the wave's shape

Wave 2 is not greenfield - it is a RECOVER-or-REBUILD decision. Every surveyor independently confirmed origin/main has none of wave-1's identity code (ServerEntry has no InstanceID/Aliases, LoadConfig has no BOM strip; git diff --stat origin/main -- internal/cli/config.go is empty). But the code is not lost - it sits fully committed on local-only branches in this checkout:

  • 68d9cbe09 (loop-epic/instance-id-identity-...) - ServerEntry.InstanceID+Aliases, ID-first keying, one-line BOM TrimPrefix, whoami extension, failing-first BOM tests.
  • 36eb52edd (loop-epic/team-aware-cli-identity-...) - bp teams / bp team use / --team, slug->UUID client-side resolve; 4/5 criteria met, only merge-gate unmet.
  • 5e941c128+07d93ccc5 (loop-epic/unifying-onboarding-bp-doctor-...) - the onboarding doctor receipt (8 sections, real read-only task_ready proof, no-bearer test).
  • All three merged clean together on wave-integration-check (tip e10410453, "Wave 1 debrief grade A-"), 18 behind / 299 ahead of origin/main, never pushed / no PR.

config.go/config_test.go are byte-untouched on main since the merge-base, so the BOM/identity hunk should cherry-pick clean; one surveyor already test-rebased the doctor branch onto current main with zero conflicts and it built. So the fastest honest path is very likely recover -> rebase per-slice onto fresh origin/main -> re-gate -> PR, NOT reimplement. The verify fleet PROVES this by actually running the rebases + gate - because "gate green" was last proven against an 18-commit-stale base, and distrust-vacuous-green forbids trusting it verbatim.

What the survey established (high confidence, multi-confirmed)

  • BP-ONB-04 code IS on origin/main. caddy.go:143 setEnvVarStep for BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL (commit 1928df610, ancestor of main); session_controller.ex + runtime.exs:77 read it; onb-w1-cloud-url-provision-inject is genuinely lifecycle_status=done. This is the ONE wave-1 slice that landed.
  • The team backend was already merged pre-wave-2 (PR 7b14b8d9): GetCredentialsForTeam (client.go:544) sets X-Barkpark-Team; cloud resolve_team/2 honors it. Team is a cloud/-only concept (Team+TeamMembership, multi-team, roles owner/admin/member), wholly separate from api/'s workspace/project/dataset tenancy - NO conflation, NO cross-table. The "biggest unknown = team-model backend" the direction flagged is effectively SOLVED; BP-ONB-02/03 is WIRING (the CLI surface), already built on the stranded branch.
  • Load-bearing team caveats: PAT auth IGNORES --team (token hard-bound to pat.team_id); only session tokens honor it. And session tokens are GLOBAL not per-team ("single-team beta", accounts.ex) - so bp team use is a client-side header preference, not a server-issued team-scoped credential. The whoami/doctor receipt must surface auth_tier + whether --team is honorable, or a PAT user is silently confused.
  • The InstanceID source exists and is already in-scope at connect. cloudclient.Barkpark.ID + .Team are resolved in finishSingleBarkpark right before connectToBarkpark(out,server,token,name) - which DROPS them. So the ID need not come from a new call; the fix widens the connect signature through SetupPlan->SavedConfig->ServerEntry. (DomainStatusResult.Instance.ID is a secondary echo, not needed at connect time.)
  • The whoami receipt is the strongest prior-art (local-first, never prints bearer) but lacks instance_id, aliases, MCP catalog version+names, read-only-call proof, reload instruction. The MCP 8-tool catalog is live on main (mcp_tasks.go). "MCP catalog version" has NO definition anywhere in the codebase - a genuine Decide design choice (cliVersion vs a hand-bumped const).

Where the survey CONTRADICTS the direction (corrections Decide must absorb)

  1. D27/D34 are not onboarding decisions. The wave-1 paper contains only D1-D7 (D4 = "identity keyed by instance ID" is the correctly-cited one). "D27 identity" belongs to the agent-onramps charter; "D34 workspace-slug resolve" belongs to the cloud-build charter - the very concurrent epic onboarding must stay file-disjoint from. Decide must NOT cite D27/D34 as wave-1 onboarding decisions.
  2. The concurrent-cycle id is mislabeled. wf_fe674ef4-19d is the CONNECTORS epic wave 6 - already MERGED into origin/main, not concurrent. The real tenancy/search cycle is bp-cloud-build-epic, slices under api/lib/barkpark/search/ + api/lib/barkpark/media/delivery/ - file-disjoint from onboarding, and both its build-slice claims are currently LAPSED with no open PR.
  3. The real collision risk is same-file, not tenancy. internal/cloudclient/client.go and internal/cli/cli.go+builtins.go are HOT - open PR #3365 (bp context-pack) touches cli.go/builtins.go. Steward must SERIALIZE onboarding's cli.go/client.go edits with #3365, not parallelize.
  4. Even recovered, the identity fix is INERT. Wave-1's own review says the ID-keying is "correct but inert - no caller stamps InstanceID." Recovery alone does NOT fix the "gyldendal-2 phantom server" bug the wish names. The connect/attach stamp (task-e6b0bc97130bae89) is genuinely fresh build work regardless of recovery.
  5. The doctor receipt FORKS whoami. The stranded implementation is a separate onboardingReceipt struct wired only to bp doctor --onboarding, violating lean choice #4 ("whoami is the single spine"). Recovery must refactor the MCP-catalog/call-proof fields onto a shared receipt builder both runWhoami and doctor call - not land the fork.

Coverage map - checked & found, and (just as loud) checked & NOT found

Found (settled - do not re-litigate)

  • config.go full map: ServerEntry struct, normalizeServerURL keying, RememberServer/FindServer/IsActiveServer/DisplayName rank-suffix (the "-2" mechanism), 3 write seams (cloud_cmd.go:241, setup_cmd.go:31, servers_cmd.go:66), LoadConfig/SaveConfig.
  • Team backend end-to-end (schemas, /v1/me, GetCredentialsForTeam, X-Barkpark-Team, resolve_team, PAT-vs-session asymmetry).
  • BP-ONB-04 on main (caddy.go:143, session_controller.ex:58-64, runtime.exs:77); the Studio button gate keys solely on :cloud_login_url.
  • whoami/servers/doctor current JSON payloads; MCP 8-tool catalog (mcp_tasks.go); cliVersion is the only version concept.
  • All stranded branches + commits located; doctor branch proven clean-rebase + build by a surveyor; CI gate identified (go-tests.yml: unscoped go vet ./... then go test -race ./...).

NOT found (absences = decisions in waiting)

  • No teams_cmd.go, no team noun in dispatch, no InstanceID/Aliases/BOM anywhere on origin/main.
  • No "MCP catalog version" concept in the codebase - Decide must invent its semantics.
  • No onboarding-composition charter file on main or in the checkout (stranded) - Decide writes it fresh via clean-extract.
  • No working bp search verb on this build - surveyors fell back to bp doc query / bp task get.
  • NOT RUN by any surveyor (the fleet's job): the actual rebase+gate of 68d9cbe09 / 36eb52edd onto current main; the real CI go test -race ./... baseline; the BOM failing-first test going red->green; the whoami/servers golden-test key assertions.
  • Corners no surveyor reached: cloudFleetPick multi-barkpark result type (does it carry ID/Team like the single path?); bake-server-image.sh env.bake block (the alt BP-ONB-04 seam); whether a genuinely fresh warm-pool provision runs CaddySteps (which stamps BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL) or only secretsInstallStep (which does not) - a direct two-surveyor CONTRADICTION.

Verify fleet - the last exploration round (8 assignments, in flight)

Each closes an unknown Decide cannot cut the plan without. Run-proofs where a claim is load-bearing; reading only where reading genuinely settles it.

  1. vf-recover-identity-bom (opus, worktree) - Rebase/cherry-pick 68d9cbe09 (ServerEntry InstanceID+Aliases + BOM strip + whoami extension) onto a fresh detached worktree off current origin/main. RUN CC=clang go build ./... && go vet ./internal/cli/... && go test ./internal/cli/... -count=1; and prove the BOM test is genuinely red on pre-fix config.go, green after. Reports: clean or exact conflicts, + gate result. The crux: recover-vs-rebuild for the identity core.
  2. vf-recover-team (opus, worktree) - Rebase 36eb52edd (bp teams / bp team use / --team) onto fresh origin/main; RUN the gate incl team tests; confirm slug->UUID resolve and non-member refusal; re-confirm GetCredentialsForTeam/X-Barkpark-Team + PAT-ignores-team are on origin/main.
  3. vf-recover-doctor-receipt (sonnet, worktree) - Rebase the doctor commits onto fresh origin/main and RUN go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestOnboarding -count=1 (shape, no-bearer, tool-call-proof-failure, MCP-catalog-matches-registration). Surveyor proved build; this proves the tests pass. Note the whoami-fork refactor cost for Decide.
  4. vf-onb04-warmpool-reconcile (opus) - Resolve the BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL contradiction: read warmpool.go's actual step assembly - does a fresh warm-pool provision run setup.CaddySteps (stamps the var) or only secretsInstallStep (does not)? RUN go test ./internal/cli/setup/ -run Caddy -count=1. Reconcile onb-w1-cloud-url-provision-inject (done) vs task-95c35d76... (open warm-pool gap). Verdict: does a new cloud customer's /login render the button, or is BP-ONB-04 still a real build?
  5. vf-connect-attach-wiring (opus) - Define the genuinely-fresh build: trace finishSingleBarkpark/finishMultiBarkpark->connectToBarkpark->SetupPlan->SavedConfig->ServerEntry and confirm only.ID/only.Team are dropped; confirm cloudFleetPick result carries ID/Team; confirm the paste-token bp setup --target connect path has no Barkpark (needs empty-ID fallback). Reading suffices.
  6. vf-gate-baseline (sonnet) - Establish the REAL green baseline: RUN CC=clang go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -race ./internal/cli/... ./internal/cloudclient/... -count=1 on clean origin/main, so any builder red is known-new.
  7. vf-whoami-golden-contract (sonnet) - Capture the exact JSON keys current tests assert: RUN go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'Whoami|Servers|Use' -count=1 and read builtins_test.go/servers_cmd_test.go, so the receipt extension lands additive-only.
  8. vf-disjointness-now (sonnet) - Confirm disjointness at build-launch: RUN gh pr list --state open --json number,title,files + scan live task claims; flag any touching config.go/servers_cmd.go/cli.go/builtins.go/cloudclient (esp. #3365) so the steward serializes merge order.

Decide — verification results, decisions & wave plan (2026-07-15)

Phase: DECIDING → BUILDING. The verify fleet came back; the surprise is that wave 2 is a RECOVER wave, not a build-fresh wave. Most of the identity work is already written and gate-green — stranded on unpushed local branches — so wave 2 re-lands it onto origin/main, activates the one inert piece, and reconciles one fork.

Verification results (proofs > facts > prose)

  • CONFIRMED — origin/main config core is bare. grep -nE "InstanceID|Aliases|TrimPrefix|0xEF" internal/cli/config.go → no matches. ServerEntry is still keyed purely by normalized URL; LoadConfig does a bare json.Unmarshal with no BOM strip. The "8/8 slices done" wave_status is FALSE against origin/main.
  • LOCATED — the wave-1 build is stranded, never pushed. Decisive proof: git merge-base --is-ancestor 68d9cbe09 HEAD → NOT ON MAIN; git branch -r --contains 68d9cbe09 → empty. Three gate-green commits carry the whole wave: 68d9cbe09 (instance-ID identity + URL aliases + BOM-tolerant config + servers/whoami fields + failing-first tests), 36eb52edd (team-aware identity — bp teams / bp team use + --team creds + Client.Me()), 5e941c128 (bp doctor --onboarding receipt). This IS the "diverged local main, never PR'd" failure the strategy predicted — now located concretely.
  • REFUTED — "the team model is the biggest unknown." The backend is fully built and merged: GetCredentialsForTeam(ctx,id,teamID) sets X-Barkpark-Team (client.go:544-554), resolve_team/2 honors it for members, /v1/me returns teams[]. The surviving work is pure CLI surface, already written on 36eb52edd. Not a design unknown — a re-land.
  • REFUTED — "no charter exists (write fresh)." A full charter existed in a worktree; it was reconciled and landed on origin/main as PR #3389 (this is now the canonical .claude/workflows/bp-onboarding-composition-charter.md).
  • REFUTED — "BP-ONB-04 warm pool skips BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL." Trace: warmpool.go:1182 iterates wp.Caddy.Steps → defaultCaddySteps.Steps → setup.CaddySteps (which includes the BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL step at caddy.go:143). Fresh provision stamps it on ALL paths; the Studio render side (session_controller.ex button) is merged. BP-ONB-04 is DONE in code — only the ops fleet backfill for pre-stamp instances (gyldendal) remains, backlogged.
  • CONFIRMED — the doctor receipt rebases cleanly. A verify pass rebased 5e941c128 onto current origin/main with zero conflicts and CC=clang go build ./... succeeded; its commits touch only cli.go/doctor_cmd.go/doctor_onboarding.go(+test), file-disjoint from everything landed since.
  • Coverage incl. not-founds: grep -rn BARKPARK_CLOUD_URL cloud/ → empty (the Elixir control plane never stamps it — the Go caddy.go side does, which the cloud-only grep missed); doctor_cmd.go composes no whoami/instance-identity today; no team/teams noun in completionNouns on main; VerifyResult.Instance does not exist (the ID source is the fleet row cloudclient.Barkpark.ID already in scope at connect, NOT a new DomainStatus call).

Decisions (mirror the charter — the charter is the epic's memory, this is the wave's story)

  • D8 RECOVER, don't rebuild. Re-land the three stranded gate-green commits onto fresh worktrees off origin/main + re-gate. Never reuse wave-integration-check wholesale (78 commits behind). Why: re-landing proven code beats a rewrite.
  • D9 Ship the activation, not just the plumbing. Slice 1 lands the config core AND wires the connect caller (finishSingleBarkpark passes Barkpark.ID+Team through connectToBarkpark→SetupPlan→SavedConfig→ServerEntry). Why: wave-1's plumbing was inert — no caller stamped an ID, so the phantom "-2" was never fixed in production.
  • D10 whoami is the single receipt spine; doctor composes over it. The receipt tail (instance_id, aliases, MCP catalog version+names, read-only call, reload) lands on the bp whoami -o json payload; bp doctor --onboarding composes over it. Why: the stranded doctor_onboarding.go forked a second receipt struct — forbidden.
  • D11 BP-ONB-04 is DONE in code; only ops backfill remains. Why: warm pool delegates to setup.CaddySteps; the button renders when cloud_login_url is set. Fleet backfill is human/ops-gated → backlog.
  • D12 'Catalog version' = cliVersion. Why: the 8-tool catalog ships in lockstep with the binary; no separate versioning scheme exists or is needed.
  • D13 File-disjoint from cloud-build W6. Onboarding touches internal/cli/** + internal/cloudclient/** only. Why: zero collision with the concurrent tenancy/search cycle.
  • D14 Serial re-land order 1 → 2 → 3. Collisions: cloud12_cmd.go (1∩2), builtins.go+cli.go (2∩3). Why: builders branch fresh, commit locally, don't push; the steward merges in order and each rebases.

Reviewer fix: localInstance was still leaving instance.id/aliases empty (built-but-inert); activated to read slice-1's stamped ServerEntry fields, prefer the entry's owning-team over the active session team, with two red-without-fix tests.

Integration proof

The three feature commits (557a87071 → 013af2330 → 999a54c24) cherry-pick onto one branch in charter order 1→2→3 with zero conflicts (cloud12_cmd.go 1∩2 and builtins.go+cli.go 2∩3 auto-merged — disjoint functions, as D14 predicted). The full integrated gate is green: CC=clang go build ./... && go vet ./internal/cli/... ./internal/cloudclient/... && go test ./internal/cli/... ./internal/cloudclient/... all pass. Integration branch HEAD 946cc752f.

The reviewer fix (D9 activation, folded from backlog)

Wave 1's lesson was "ship the activation, not just the plumbing." The whoami spine landed with localInstance reading only URL/name/team — instance.id and instance.aliases stayed empty even after slice 1 makes ServerEntry.InstanceID/Aliases available. The wish explicitly names "instance ID … URL+aliases" as receipt fields, so leaving them inert would repeat the exact wave-1 failure. Fixed in place on the integrated branch: whoami's network-free instance block now reads the stamped identity. This folds the whoami half of onb-backlog-doctor-prefer-local-serverentry; the doctor-path offline optimization (point onboardingInstance at local config instead of the live fleet fetch) remains in that backlog task.

Ledger audit

All three slice tasks + the folded task-e6b0bc97130bae89 are honestly stamped: lifecycle in_progress (NOT closed — the merge-gated "PR merged" criterion stays open with empty evidence for the lead to close on merge), every proven criterion carries file:line/test evidence stamped as the work happened, and the claim now-lines reflect "gate green, committing to local branch." No task outside this wave was touched. The backlog task onb-backlog-doctor-prefer-local-serverentry was updated to record that the whoami half landed in wave 2.

Grade — A

Genuinely strong: the recovery is faithful (no rewrite drift), every load-bearing test is protective (BOM red-without-strip, connect-seam collapse, X-Barkpark-Team value end-to-end, no-bearer with distinct seeded secrets, live MCP catalog match, 403-not-rubber-stamped), the code is idiomatic and thoroughly commented, and the slices cohere into one zero-conflict wave. The reviewer activation closes the one real gap against the wish (the receipt now carries the instance ID + aliases it promises). Held short of A+ only because the doctor path still round-trips the live fleet for instance identity (offline/local-first optimization deferred) and the BOM strip covers UTF-8 only (UTF-16 still bricks — acceptable, Windows emits UTF-8). Nothing here is bloat; every slice composes a merged primitive as the charter's D2 demands.

What the next wave should take

The identity transaction is complete in code. Next: (a) the LEAD merges 1→2→3 (or merges wave2-integration as the wave) and closes the four merge-gated criteria; (b) the deferred command-discovery classification (BP-ONB-07), fleet-health decompose (BP-ONB-09 CLI half), and onramp BOM/tracker safety (BP-ONB-12 onramp + 14) are the filed backlog→wave candidates; (c) the BP-ONB-04 ops fleet backfill (onb-backlog-cloud-url-fleet-backfill) stays human/ops-gated. The whole epic then rests on live end-to-end proof of the sub-5-minute Windows journey against a real Cloud instance.
